''Citharexylum quadrangulare'' [[Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin|Jacq.]] | synonyms_ref = {{GRIN | access-date=2010-12-13}} }} '''''Citharexylum spinosum''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Verbenaceae]] that is native to southern [[Florida]] in the [[United States]], the [[Caribbean]], [[Guyana]], [[Suriname]], and [[Venezuela]]. Common names include '''Florida fiddlewood''' and '''spiny fiddlewood'''. ==Description== It is a [[tree]] that reaches a height of up to {{convert|15|m|ft|abbr=on}}. The ovate to elliptic leaves are {{convert|4|-|20|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and have orange [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. Small white flowers are produced throughout the year on hanging axillary and terminal [[raceme]]s and [[panicle]]s {{convert|20|-|40|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length. The fruit are red to black subglobose [[drupe]]s {{convert|7|-|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter.{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/tropicalornament00wart |url-access=registration |title=Tropical Ornamentals: a Guide |first=W.
